external_collaboration.evidence_quote: Monique Berger graduated from VU Amsterdam with a degree in Human Kinetic Sciences. From 1993, Monique has held various positions within the Human Kinetic Technology degree programme and worked as a senior researcher at the Rehabilitation Research Group. From this degree programme, she shaped the research in the Human Kinetic Technology Centre of Expertise. Many of these projects are aimed at adapted sports and wheelchair sports in particular. The joint research groups with Basalt Rehabilitation, Rehabilitation & Technology and Assistive Technology for Mobility and Sports, have been renewed for a new six-year term.
Through the Framerunner project, The Hague University of Applied Sciences works with local partners in Tanzania on solutions for people with mobility impairments.

Rienk van der Slikke specializes in the use of wearables to evaluate wheelchair performance. Primarily within wheelchair sport, but also in applications within rehabilitation, such as around the partnership with Basalt. He does this within the HHS and with appointments at TU Delft, Loughborough University and NOC*NSF.

Liliya Terzieva is Professor Designing Value Networks as well as Director of the Centre of Expertise Mission Zero. Next to the above, she is a visiting professor of the University of Montpellier, France and of the University of National and World Economy in Sofia, Bulgaria. Her PhD is in the Economic and Organizational sciences of Leisure and Tourism.
